subject: Prior for standard deviations of group-level ('random') effects

messages.author: 426a499784c7cca0
messages.subject: Prior for standard deviations of group-level ('random') effects
parts:
Hi,
i am running a model where i set the prior for the sd as a default student t distribution (3 degrees of freedom, centered at 0, and with a scale parameter  that depends on the standard deviation of the response). I was wondering whether the 3 degrees of freedom are still correct if my sample size is 20. Have i to change it to 19 and specify the grouping factor?

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Prior for standard deviations of group-level ('random') effects
parts:
My choice to use 3 DF as the default has nothing to do with the size of your data on you don't need to change it based on this.

The reason I am using 3 DF is because I want the tail of the prior to be reasonably wide (in partricular wider than the tails of the normal distribution), while not running into sampling problems at the same time: A t distribution with 1 or 2 DFs might sometimes lead to problems in sampling because it is too wide. Hence the choice of DF = 3.
